metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: Vehicle locations extracted from traffic video frames and reformed as position matrices, used as input to the DRL method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available upon request from the corresponding author, but no public link or specific identifier.

nodes_source.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_source.description: Data used to calibrate simulation parameters related to driving behaviors.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available upon request from the corresponding author, but no public link or specific identifier.

nodes_source.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method... determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on... the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_source.description: Traffic measurements, specifically downstream occupancies, used as input for the PI-ALINEA method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available upon request from the corresponding author, but no public link or specific identifier.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations are extracted as (x,y) points from raw traffic video frames.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, no tools or params named for extraction.

nodes_process.node_name: Represent Traffic State as Position Matrices
nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m_t E R^XxY; m_t(x, y) = U_v, i E I_t,
nodes_process.description: Vehicle location points are reformed into position matrices. Each matrix element (x,y) is set to a constant Uv if a vehicle is present at that location, otherwise zero.

nodes_process.node_name: Embed Signal State Information into Position Matrices
nodes_process.source_quote: The position matrix additionally contains the information of the signal states: m_t(X_R, Y_R) = {U_G, if a_{t-1} = G, U_R, if a_{t-1} = R,
nodes_process.description: The position matrix is updated to include signal state information (green or red) at a specific signal light position (XR, YR), using constants UG and UR.

nodes_process.source_quote: For computation efficiency, down-sampling is intro-duced before the matrix stack to reduce the input dimen-sions and maintain sufficient information about vehicle positions.
nodes_process.description: Position matrices are down-sampled to reduce input dimensions while retaining vehicle position information. The size of one observation after down-sampling is 4x512 pixels.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, some params stated, but method missing.

nodes_process.node_name: Stack Down-sampled Matrices into State Sequence
nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s_t: S_t = {m_{t-(N-1)},..., m_t}.
nodes_process.description: Matrices of N consecutive time steps are stacked to form the traffic state S_t, capturing vehicle dynamics. Three consecutive observations are stacked.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 param stated, no tools named.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r_t after action a_t is defined by the following: r_t = μv_t + ωq_t, μ > 0, ω < 0,
nodes_process.description: The reward function combines average speed in the merging area (v_t) and average queue length at the on-ramp (q_t) with positive weight mu and negative weight omega, balancing vehicle mobility and delay.

nodes_process.node_name: Initialize Q-network and Target Network Weights
nodes_process.source_quote: Initialize the action-value function Q with random weights w. Initialize the target network Q-with weights w- = w
nodes_process.description: The weights of the deep neural Q-network are initialized randomly. A separate target network Q- is also initialized with the same weights as the Q-network.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no tools named, random_seed not stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Traffic simulation is set up using SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator. The simulation models a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao, including an on-ramp, mainline, and merging area. Speed limits are 80 km/h (mainline) and 40 km/h (on-ramp). Simulation time is 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. Driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 1/1 tool named, all params stated. Some simulation details remain unstated.

nodes_process.source_quote: the Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: The Q-network architecture is a revised version of Mnih et al. [30]'s network, comprising three CNN layers and one FC layer per output. The input is a 3x4x512 tensor. CNN layers have specific filters, sizes, and strides. Total 2 million weights.

nodes_process.node_name: Train Deep Q-network with Multitask Learning
nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1. The ramp meter takes new action with the e-greedy strategy...
nodes_process.description: The Q-network is trained using deep Q-learning with experience replay and a target network. It employs an epsilon-greedy strategy for action selection and Adam optimizer for weight updates. A multitask learning strategy predicts speed and queue length simultaneously, using a total loss function (L = L1 + lambda*L2).
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 2/6 tools named, all params stated. Some general RL tools not named from specific libraries.

nodes_process.source_quote: The first scenario does not apply ramp metering
nodes_process.description: Traffic simulation is run without any ramp metering control to establish a baseline for comparison.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/1 tool named, random_seed not stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method.
nodes_process.description: Traffic simulation is run using the PI-ALINEA method, which fixes green phase length and determines red phase length based on previous cycle's red phase and downstream occupancies. Formula: rk = rk-1 + KR[ok - ô] - Kp[ok-1 - ok].
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/2 tools named, most params stated, random_seed not stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed DRL method results in (1) lower travel times in the mainline, (2) shorter vehicle queues at the on-ramp, and (3) higher traffic flows downstream of the merging area.
nodes_process.description: The trained DRL model is applied in the simulated traffic environment. Key performance indicators are measured, including mainline travel times, on-ramp queue lengths, and downstream traffic flows. These results are then used for comparison with baseline scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 1/2 tools named, random_seed not stated.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate and Compare Mean Vehicle Travel Times
nodes_process.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simu-lation experiments. It is found that the performance of the PI-ALINEA method is not always better than that of the no-control scenario.
nodes_process.description: Mean vehicle travel times from 20 simulation experiments for the DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios are compared and presented.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, some params stated, but no specific tools mentioned for analysis/plotting.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate and Compare Temporal-Spatial Speed Distribution
nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline. The results further demonstrate the efficiency of the ramp metering and the better performance of the proposed method.
nodes_process.description: Temporal-spatial distributions of mean speeds along the mainline are compared for DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios, presented as heatmaps.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no specific tools or params mentioned for visualization.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate and Compare On-Ramp Queue Lengths
nodes_process.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_process.description: On-ramp queue lengths, including Q1, Q2, and Q3 percentiles, are evaluated and compared across DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no specific tools or params mentioned for analysis/visualization.

nodes_process.node_name: Evaluate and Compare Downstream Traffic Flows
nodes_process.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_process.description: Traffic flows downstream of the merging area are evaluated and compared for DRL, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, no specific tools or params mentioned for visualization.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: A perturbation analysis is performed to assess the impact of video data information. The control area is divided into eight subareas. Information from specific subareas is removed from the original data to generate perturbed data, and travel times are re-evaluated.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, 1/2 tools named, all params stated, but details of 'information removal' are vague.
